title: Déhanche Week 0 Report — Mousa Batarseh
description: An independent Week 0 e-commerce report on dehanche.com by Mousa Batarseh: twelve flags with evidence, a catalog scanner run on all 164 live products, a revenue pacing board, email flow concepts, a test roadmap, a launch checklist, and worked examples on revenue targets, hourly pacing, Klaviyo segments, bundles, developer briefs and the weekly note.

blocks.text: Your first weekly report, before day one.

The eComm Manager job asks for a weekly note that says what happened, why, where we are against target, and what we'll do. I don't have your numbers yet, so I read everything else. This is dehanche.com as it rendered on September 16, 2026, every one of its 164 live products run through a catalog check, and the tools I'd run the role with.
Product images with their own alt text
Public storefront only: product JSON, collection pages, sitemap, rendered pages on mobile and desktop. No login, no internal data.
THE REPORT · FOUR PARTS, AS THE POSTING ASKS
Same format I'd send every Monday. This week's version is built from what a customer, a search engine and a scraper can see.

The Fall 2026 drop is live and the product pages read beautifully. Underneath, the storefront has drifted: a sold-out belt in a top slot, a “Pre-Order” page selling sale stock, three copies of All Belts, and tags that contradict the product.
Each of these costs clicks, trust or rankings, and none needs a developer to fix. Most trace back to product data: tags, types and alt text feed the filters, feeds, search and email segments.
Unknown from the outside. Below is the pacing board I'd set up on day one, running on sample numbers until it's connected to Shopify.

This week: fix slot order, retire the Pre-Order page, redirect the duplicate collections, start the tag-to-metafield cleanup. Next: the size-row and second-belt tests, then two new email flows with the Klaviyo team.
PDP titles and descriptions are specific and on-brand: “Hollyhock Black Silver Belt | Déhanche”, cast in Italy, ten holes, lined in suede.
516 of 631 size variants are in stock and only 4 of 164 products are fully sold out. There's plenty of product to merchandise.
The theme already knows “Available”, “Low Availability” and “Pre-Order” per size, and has Klaviyo waitlist hooks wired in.
Algolia search, Rebuy recommendations, Global-e, Klaviyo, Clarity, Triple Whale. Nothing new to buy, just tuning.
Free US ground shipping over $250 and 15% off two full-price belts are both good AOV levers.
The imagery and storytelling carry the brand. The fixes below should protect that, not dilute it.
Each flag shows what I saw, why it costs sales or trust, and the fix. Everything was captured from the public storefront on September 16, 2026. Screenshots are cropped, not edited.
A sold-out belt sits in slot 10 of All Belts. The $250 best sellers sit at 33 and 34.
The first three rows take most of the clicks. A sold-out tile there is a dead end, and Constance at $250 is the easiest first purchase in the line.

Sold-out products drop to the end automatically, and their tile offers the waitlist instead. In-stock best sellers at each price tier ($250 / $290 / $325) are pinned into the first twelve slots. I'd review the order weekly against sell-through.
collection CTR, PDP views per session

blocks.alt: All Belts collection grid on dehanche.com with a Sold Out tile for Hollyhock Crystal Black Silver in the third row
blocks.caption: Third row of All Belts, desktop: the Sold Out tile next to an in-stock croco Hollyhock.

blocks.text: The “Pre-Order” page is selling final-sale stock.

A shopper who lands here from search, an old email or an ad reads “pre-order” and expects to wait. Instead they get in-stock belts, some of them final sale and non-returnable. The posting names this exact problem: an in-stock product showing as pre-order.

Let inventory drive pre-order status. The theme already reads a per-size Pre-Order state from Fabrikator. Rebuild the collection as “tag Preorder AND not in stock”, remove the tag from styles that have shipped, and redirect the page to New Arrivals whenever it's empty.

blocks.alt: Mobile view of the dehanche.com Pre-Order collection showing two SALE items with struck-through prices
blocks.caption: Mobile, Sept 16: “PRE-ORDER” heading above two SALE tiles.

blocks.text: “New Arrivals” goes back almost a year.
Regulars stop checking “New” when it doesn't change, and the Fall 2026 pieces get buried among older ones.
Make the collection automatic: published in the last 60 days, in stock. Pin the hero launch pieces by hand and drop the manual tag.
Filters, the Google feed, search and email segments all read these tags. A karat filter that returns silver belts loses trust, and conflicting karat data is a product-claims risk on a luxury site.

Move product facts into metafields with one allowed value each: metal (Silver / 24K gold-plated / Mixed), leather, width, collection family. Tags stay for merchandising only. Internal tags get an underscore prefix and a written owner, so the next person knows what's safe to delete. The scanner below lists every affected product.
Gaps in product records break the tools downstream.
Product type drives Google Shopping categories and category reporting. Zero weights can misprice shipping and Global-e duty quotes. Missing SKUs break inventory syncs and wholesale reconciliation.
One bulk CSV pass (Matrixify or the Shopify bulk editor), plus a required-fields check before any product goes live. That check is item one on the launch checklist below.
Every image of a product says the same thing.
products.json · Hollyhock Black Silver product page HTML

Screen-reader shoppers hear the same name eighteen times. Google Images, a real discovery channel for visual luxury goods, gets one repeated phrase. Feeds read the empty field, and missing or identical alt text often appears in ADA demand letters.

Fill alt text from a template in one bulk pass: “Hollyhock belt in black calfskin with silver five-ring hardware, front view”, then “…, worn at the waist”, and so on. Add it to the launch checklist so new products ship with it.
Google Images clicks in Search Console
Three “All Belts” pages compete with each other.
Google splits ranking signals across near-duplicates and can pick the copy to rank.
301 /all-belts-copy to /belts. Keep /belts-all (the full-price view) out of the index, or give it a distinct purpose and title. One All Belts page holds the rankings.
Internal and expired collections are public and in the sitemap.
61 collections in sitemap_collections · page titles as served
Empty and internal pages sit in the index, shoppers can reach them, and old seasons can outrank the current one.

Unpublish the utility collections from the Online Store, or noindex them through the template. Redirect past seasons to the current season, hold Resort 2027 until launch day, and audit collections once a quarter.
The homepage title is only the brand name.
Title: “Déhanche | Sculptural Italian Leather Belts & Jewelry”, and a clean H1. It takes two minutes and lets the homepage rank for more than the brand name.
Size is the first question about a belt, and the product page hides it.
only after tapping Add to Cart
Shoppers who can't see their size or its stock before committing hesitate. “Only one left in XL” works as urgency only if people see it.
Show the size row with stock state above Add to Cart (A/B test, T1 below). Fix the badge's z-index. Test an installment line on items over $250.

blocks.alt: Mobile product page with the Find my fit size sheet open after tapping Add to Cart
blocks.caption: Sizes appear in a sheet after Add to Cart.

blocks.alt: Close-up of the mobile header where the Bestseller label overlaps the search, account and bag icons
blocks.caption: “BESTSELLER” overlapping the header icons.

blocks.text: The best offer on the site only shows in the top banner.
no progress bar and no second-belt prompt
The offer is there to raise order value, but no one sees it when they add a first belt, which is when it would matter.

Add a bag nudge: “Add a second belt, save 15%”, with Rebuy suggestions limited to in-stock sizes and the other hardware finish of the same style. Test a shoppable Hollyhock row under the hero against the editorial layout (T2 and T5).
Heavy pages: three copies of one 1080p video, a doubled GA4 tag, 30+ third parties.
Lighthouse 12, mobile, lab run from a cloud server (directional) · page source · resource timing
Luxury traffic arrives mostly on phones, from Instagram and email, and a slow first product page loses sales. A doubled GA4 tag can also double-count, which undermines the weekly numbers.

Load the video once, at 720p on mobile with a poster image. Consolidate to one GTM container, remove unused pixels (why is Yandex Metrica there?), and delay below-the-fold apps. Confirm the gains with field data (Search Console Core Web Vitals, CrUX) before and after.

Priority adds up issue weights: high 5, medium 3, low 1. The rules mirror flags 01–08. Product names and data come from dehanche.com's public product feed.
Where are we against target, today?

The posting asks for daily and hourly pacing against weekly and monthly targets. This is the board I'd build in the first week. Every number here is a sample until it's connected to Shopify and your real targets; change the inputs to see how it responds.
Pace is weighted by day of week, heavier on weekends and email-send days, rather than split evenly across the month.
SHOW THE NUMBERS AS A TABLE
Flow 06 trigger met: more than 8% behind pace after the 15th. Today's options, with sample estimates of what each could recover:

items:
1.
Send flow 06 to engaged non-buyers (best sellers, full size runs)
≈ $6.6K

2.
Put the second-belt nudge in the bag (test T2)
≈ $2.3K

3.
Swap the homepage to an in-stock Hollyhock row
≈ $1.9K

4.
Email waitlists for sizes that came back
≈ $1.5K

5.
Move sold-out tiles out of the top rows
≈ $950

blocks.text: EMAIL · SIX FLOW CONCEPTS FOR THE KLAVIYO TEAM
Use sales data to time every send.

The posting asks the eComm Manager to use real-time sales, product and customer data to shape email. These are six places where that data changes what gets sent and when. All are concepts to build with the email team, using products and prices from the live site.

items:
Trigger: a back-in-stock request for one size.
e.g. Constance Black Silver, size S, sold out today

Email when that size restocks. Subject: “Your size is back: Constance, S”.
instant

Reminder only if the shopper hasn't bought and two or fewer are left: “Two left in S”.
+24 hours
Exit when they order that size.

Skip anyone with a return or exchange open; send at most once every 90 days.

A short, specific email with one action.

Subject: Your size is back: Constance, S
Preview: Constance Black Silver · S · back in stock today.
It names the exact size, shows one product, and has one button that opens the page with size S already selected. It doesn't discount the belt.
Its value is measured as revenue per back-in-stock request, and it's only a good report number if flag 01's waitlist tiles are feeding it.
CONCEPT · WRITTEN BY MOUSA FOR THIS APPLICATION
Your size is back: Constance, S
You asked us to tell you. Constance Black Silver in S is available again, in small numbers.
Free US ground shipping over $250 · Handmade in Italy

Scored with ICE (impact, confidence, ease; 1–10 each). Each test has one metric, a guardrail and a named audience. Sort by any column. I've run A/B and conversion tests before, and this is the list I'd start from.

rows: T3 In-stock first on All Belts
Moving sold-out and broken size runs down lifts collection click-through.
T2 Second-belt nudge in the bag
Surfacing the live 15%-off-two offer when a first belt is added lifts units per order.
Units per order · guardrail: margin per order
T1 Size row visible on the product page
Showing sizes and stock before Add to Cart lifts adds and cuts size exchanges.
Showing per-size low stock on the page creates honest urgency.
Add-to-cart on low-stock sizes · guardrail: returns
An Afterpay/Klarna line under the price eases hesitation on $300+ belts.
T7 Free-shipping progress in the bag
A progress line to $250 moves $190–$240 carts over the threshold.
T5 Shoppable Hollyhock row on the homepage
A product row under the hero shortens the path from home to product.
Home → PDP rate · guardrail: bounce rate
T8 “Wear it with” in the same finish
Jewelry in the belt's hardware finish on belt pages raises jewelry attach.
Jewelry attach rate · guardrail: belt conversion

The posting asks for launches that are prepared, tested and correct. This checklist would run before every drop. Ticks are saved in this browser, so you can try it.
WORKED EXAMPLES · THE REST OF THE POSTING
Seven more lines from the job, worked through.

Each tab takes one responsibility from the posting and shows how I'd handle it at Déhanche. Prices, the two-belt offer and the $250 shipping line come from dehanche.com on September 16. Traffic, order and customer numbers are samples, and marked that way, until they come from Shopify, GA4 and Klaviyo.

FROM THE POSTING
Own daily and hourly revenue pacing against monthly and weekly sales targets
Revenue is sessions × conversion × order value. A target only becomes workable once it's split into those three, because each has different owners and different fixes.
On its own, any one lever would need +3.6%: 124,378 sessions, or 0.69% conversion, or $373 per order. Spread across all three, it's +1.2% each.
CLOSE THE GAP: PICK THE MOVES
Merge the three All Belts pages and rewrite the homepage title
Two extra sends a month to engaged browsers
Keep New Arrivals current so paid social lands on in-stock product
Size row with stock state on the product page
Sold-out tiles out of the top rows
Lighter mobile pages: one video, one Tag Manager
“Wear it with” jewelry in the same finish
The lift on each move is a planning assumption, not a promise. In the first month I'd replace these with Déhanche's own test results and last year's numbers.
THE MONTHLY TARGET, SPLIT BY WEEK
Learn it, fix it, then grow it.
The first month is for learning the business and fixing what's clearly broken. Targets get set once I've seen the real numbers.

blocks.text: I've spent seven years running e-commerce storefronts end to end, including Shopify stores for apparel and textile brands. I look for problems before anyone reports them, and I'd like to do that for Déhanche.

items:
SHOPIFY
Built and ran Shopify and WooCommerce stores for two apparel and textile brands (Universal Wholesale & United Textile, 2019–2023): catalogs of 14,000+ SKUs, collections, launches, promo calendars.

MERCHANDISING
Homepage, collection and navigation merchandising around launches; product data, pricing, inventory and imagery, owned end to end.

NOW
Webmaster at Wild Bill's Tobacco (2023–now): the wholesale e-commerce site and a portfolio of retail sites, campaign pages and launch readiness with marketing.

TESTING
I've run A/B and conversion tests, and I work from GA4, Search Console and PageSpeed data.

SEARCH
Took organic rankings to Google pages 1–2 within a year; I handle redirects, metadata and site hygiene myself.

EDUCATION
B.S., Accounting Information Systems. Bilingual English and Arabic.
